blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: immediate — Operand value encoded as a literal.
direct — Memory address of data specified in instruction.
indirect — Specified memory holds a further effective address.
indexed — Base address modified by index or displacement.
effective address — Final memory location used for operand access.

blocks.title: Literal versus location
blocks.text: Immediate addressing embeds a literal value; direct addressing points to the memory address holding a value.

blocks.title: Follow a pointer for indirect
blocks.text: M[21] contains 20, so an indirect read through address 21 accesses M[20]=7.

blocks.title: Calculate indexed address
blocks.text: Base 20 plus index X=2 gives effective address 22 and value 3. These operand formats are generic examples rather than LMC syntax.

blocks.title: Worked example · Predict
blocks.text: Immediate is literal 6; direct gets 4 from memory address 30.

blocks.title: Worked example · Explain
blocks.text: Indirect follows pointer 30 stored at 31 to value 4; indexed adds offset 2 to base 30 to read 9.
